analysis:
Examined all supplied metadata, patches and source excerpts. These units change documentation, not executable controls; no concrete security regression is established. README adds navigation; the changelog and architecture describe authenticated local hold IPC, persistent leases/locks, bounded cancellation, model unloading, deferred updates and Autopilot refusal (docs/architecture/model-autopilot.md:182–184). Existing consent, model verification and memory safeguards remain documented.

The new socket/operator-mailbox boundary affects TB-003 and availability; integration should verify AddonPeerPolicy/AddonIPCServer signer and same-user authentication, path protection, request bounds, persistence and release authority. docs/developer/test.md:788–790 explicitly limits peer-policy testing to rejection and substitutes authentication in successful flows; signed add-on interoperation remains unverified, not evidence of a bypass.

docs/architecture/addon-hold.md:35–82 describes cross-file drain ownership, cancellation (T-010), cache retirement (T-028/T-041), reconnect and App Attest continuity (T-053/T-057). Implementation review must ensure release does not restore serving under expired/revoked authorization, deferred loads remain fenced, and retained native work is not treated as retired. Lines 91 and 93 document residency after retirement failure and unheld startup after unreadable persistence: reconcile these with VM handoff and machine-lock enforcement before concluding resource safety. They alone do not establish exploitable implementation behavior.

Also verify hold/update and App Attest stall-recovery interactions (lines 54–64), and draining exclusion across registration/heartbeat on the actual coordinator. The changelog:16–17 states busy-field support ships separately; that is an external compatibility contract, not proof of a routing regression. No supplied change exposes prompts, keys or receipts or alters encryption/billing; busy-addon telemetry and the local transition log need implementation-level data-minimization review. Canonical detail is selective, and the referenced implementations are outside this batch.
